mainTopic: Blood and juices given out by roasting and salting: the knife-pressure distinction, fish salted with birds, and kosher meat salted with טרפה meat
overview: This amud opens with the last word of an earlier instruction: tilt the vessel to pour the fat off the drippings from roasting meat. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא challenges רב אשי by setting two statements of שמואל against each other. שמואל holds that roasted meat whose redness is gone no longer gives out blood, yet he forbids a loaf of bread that roasted meat was cut on. רב אשי answers that the pressure of the knife squeezes out extra blood. Next, רב נחמן rules that fish and birds salted together are forbidden. The גמרא explains that the case is a vessel with holes: the soft-skinned fish finish giving out their blood first, and then they absorb the blood the hard-skinned birds are still giving out. Finally, kosher meat salted together with טרפה meat is brought to רבא. He forbids it, learning from the word "הטמאים" that the juice of non-kosher meat is also forbidden.

steps.title: Finishing the instruction: tilt the vessel to pour off the fat
steps.stepSummary: The last word of an earlier instruction: after the drippings collect, one tilts the vessel to pour off the fat.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes an instruction that started before this section, about collecting what drips from roasting meat. You gently tilt the vessel so the fat pours off without the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier instruction had salt placed in the vessel under the roasting meat, so the blood sticks to the salt and the fat floats on top. Tilting lets you pour the fat into another vessel without mixing in the blood. This sets up the next challenge about whether such meat still gives out blood at all.

keyTerms.meaning: and he tilts it (gently pours it off)

phrases.english: And he tilts it.
phrases.notes: This finishes an instruction from before: tilt the vessel so the fat floating on top pours off without the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a practical instruction that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gently tilt the vessel to pour off the fat separately from the blood.

steps.title: Did שמואל really say that? The loaf of bread cut with meat
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא challenges רב אשי by pointing to another ruling of שמואל, which seems to say roasted meat still holds blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא said to רב אשי: Did שמואל really say this? But שמואל said that a loaf of bread on which one cut meat is forbidden to eat!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges what שמואל was quoted as saying. Another ruling of שמואל seems to show that roasted meat still lets out blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ruling assumed that once roasted meat loses its redness, no more blood comes out. But שמואל also forbade a loaf that roasted meat was cut on. That ruling only makes sense if blood still comes out of the meat, so the two statements of שמואל seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (a formula that challenges a quoted ruling)
But didn't he say? (brings a clashing statement)
a loaf of bread

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Ika said to Rav Ashi:
And did Shmuel really say this?
phrases.notes: "This" means that once the meat's redness is gone, it no longer gives out blood.

phrases.english: But didn't Shmuel say:
A loaf on which one cut meat
is forbidden to eat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind the instruction just finished.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that roasted meat whose redness is gone no longer gives out blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forbidding a loaf that roasted meat was cut on assumes the meat still gives out blood, which contradicts the first ruling.

steps.title: The knife's pressure squeezes out blood
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the loaf case is different, because pressing with the knife pushes blood out of the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the pressure of the knife makes the meat give out blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that the two rulings do not clash. When you cut the meat, the knife presses on it and squeezes blood out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, meat whose redness is gone does not drip blood, so the first ruling stands. Cutting is different, because the knife pushes down and forces out blood that would not come out by itself. That blood lands on the loaf, which is why the loaf is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different there (a formula that splits two cases apart)
because of, by means of
the pressure of the knife
gives out, releases (blood or juice)

steps.whatToRemember: Meat whose redness is gone does not give out blood on its own, but pressing on it, as a knife does, can squeeze blood out.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because through the pressure of the knife it gives out [blood].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing the two cases are not alike.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbidding the loaf seemed to prove that roasted meat always still gives out blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: Roasted meat gives out blood only when pressed, as by a knife, so both rulings of שמואל hold.

steps.title: רב נחמן: fish and birds salted together are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that fish and birds salted together are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says: Fish and birds that one salted together are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. רב נחמן gives a rule about salting fish and birds together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salting draws blood out. Fish blood is permitted, but bird blood is forbidden. רב נחמן says that salting the two together makes them forbidden, but he does not yet say in what kind of vessel or why, and the גמרא will ask about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: fish
birds (fowl)
salting meat to draw out its blood

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּגִים וְעוֹפוֹת שֶׁמְּלָחָן זֶה עִם זֶה –
phrases.english: Fish and birds that one salted together,
are forbidden.
phrases.notes: The answer later shows that it is the fish that get forbidden, from soaking up the birds' blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: דָּגִים וְעוֹפוֹת שֶׁמְּלָחָן זֶה עִם זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about blood coming out of meat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish salted together with birds are forbidden.

steps.title: What case? Neither kind of vessel seems to fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רב נחמן means. In a vessel without holes, even two birds would be forbidden. In a vessel with holes, even fish and birds should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it is in a vessel without holes, then even birds with birds should be forbidden. If it is in a vessel with holes, then even fish with birds should be permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to picture רב נחמן's case and runs into trouble either way. Neither type of vessel seems to explain why only fish with birds is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a vessel without holes, the blood pools and everything in it soaks it up, so mixing in fish should not matter. In a vessel with holes, the blood drains away, so nothing should absorb it. Either way, singling out fish with birds seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: what are the circumstances? (asks to define the case)
a vessel with holes, so the blood drains out
a vessel without holes, so the blood pools inside
permitted

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If in a vessel without holes,
then even birds with birds should also be forbidden,
If in a vessel with holes,
then even fish with birds should also be permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי בִּכְלִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְנוּקָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רב נחמן's ruling could make sense in any kind of vessel.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that fish salted with birds are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vessel without holes would forbid even birds with birds, and a vessel with holes would permit even fish with birds, so the ruling seems to have no case.

steps.title: A vessel with holes, but the timing differs
steps.stepSummary: The case is a vessel with holes. Fish have soft skin and finish giving out their blood first, but the birds' hard skin makes them keep giving out blood, which the fish then absorb.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is in a vessel with holes. Fish have soft skin, so they give out their blood first. Birds have hard skin. After the fish finish, the birds are still giving out blood, and then the fish absorb it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן means a vessel with holes. The problem is timing: fish finish giving out their blood quickly, while birds take longer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While something is still giving out its own blood, it does not absorb blood from outside. Fish, with soft skin, finish early, and once they stop they start absorbing the blood the slower birds are still giving out. Two birds give out blood at the same pace, so neither absorbs from the other, which explains why only fish with birds is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually (keeps one option and explains it)
their skin is soft
tight, hard (skin)
they absorb

steps.whatToRemember: Fish salted with birds become forbidden even in a vessel with holes. The fish finish giving out their blood first, then absorb the blood the birds are still giving out.
steps.confusionAlert: It is the fish that become forbidden, not the birds. Birds salted with other birds are fine, because they all give out blood at the same pace.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the idea that something still giving out blood does not absorb blood, and that the timing of giving out blood decides whether absorption happens.

phrases.english: Really, it is in a vessel with holes,
and the fish, because their skin is soft,
give out [their blood] first,
while birds are tight-skinned,
after the fish have settled down,
phrases.notes: Literally "rested." It means the fish have finished giving out their blood.

phrases.english: the birds give out [blood],
and then [the fish] absorb from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by choosing the vessel with holes and explaining the difference in timing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case, with an explanation based on how the foods behave
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In a vessel with holes the blood drains away, so the fish should stay permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in a vessel with holes, the fish finish first and then absorb the birds' later blood, so they are forbidden. Birds with birds are permitted because they give out blood at the same time.

steps.title: Kosher meat salted with טרפה meat is brought to רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בר רחל had kosher slaughtered meat salted together with טרפה meat, and he brought the case to רבא for a ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי בר רחל had kosher slaughtered meat that was salted together with טרפה meat. He came before רבא to ask about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real case that was brought to רבא. This sets up רבא's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kosher meat and טרפה meat were salted together in the usual way, and both give out liquid during salting. Step 6 taught that something still giving out its own blood does not absorb, so perhaps the kosher meat took in nothing from the טרפה meat. The story does not spell out the question; bringing the case to רבא is the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat from an animal that had a kosher slaughtering
Meat from an animal with a deadly injury or defect, which is forbidden
Was salted (the salting done to draw blood out of meat)

phrases.english: Rav Mari bar Raḥel
had meat of a slaughtered animal salted for him
together with meat of a טרפה,
he came before Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל אִימְּלַח לֵיהּ בְּשַׂר שְׁחוּטָה בַּהֲדֵי בְּשַׂר טְרֵפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the theory about one food absorbing from another during salting (fish and birds), the גמרא brings a practical case of kosher and טרפה meat salted together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is kosher meat that was salted together with טרפה meat forbidden?

steps.title: רבא forbids the meat because the juice of non-kosher food is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the word "הטמאים" that the Torah forbids the juice, gravy and spices of non-kosher food, so the kosher meat that absorbed the טרפה juice is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: The פסוק says "the unclean" to teach that their juice, their gravy and their spices are also forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question with a source from the Torah. The juice that comes out of the טרפה meat is forbidden, and the kosher meat absorbed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word "the" in "הטמאים" adds that the prohibition covers more than the meat itself. It also covers the juice that comes out during salting, the gravy, and the spices cooked with it. Since the kosher meat took in the טרפה juice, the kosher meat is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: "The unclean": the Torah's word for forbidden creatures, which is used here to add more prohibitions
Juice or liquid that comes out of meat or fish, for example during salting
Gravy or cooking liquid
Spices or bits of seasoning cooked together with the food

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that the kosher meat is safe just because it is busy giving out its own blood. רבא's point is that the טרפה juice still gets into it and makes it forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source that the forbidden status of non-kosher food also applies to the liquids that come out of it. That is why kosher meat salted together with non-kosher meat becomes forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Kosher meat salted together with טרפה meat is forbidden. The Torah's word "הטמאים" makes the טרפה's juice, gravy and spices forbidden, and the kosher meat absorbs that juice.

phrases.english: He said to him: "The unclean"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:31. רבא learns from the extra word "the" that something more is included.

phrases.english: comes to forbid their juice,
and their gravy, and their spices.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the case from step 7 using a source from a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The kosher meat is forbidden, because the Torah forbids the juice of non-kosher meat, and the kosher meat absorbed that juice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The juice, gravy and spices of non-kosher creatures are forbidden, learned from the word "הטמאים".
